module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Partitions of $n$ into distinct non-squarefree parts for $n > 23$

a: Number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts that are not squarefree.
This is the number of finite subsets of positive integers $P$ such that
$\sum_{k \in P} k = n$ and every element $k \in P$ is not squarefree.

*References:*
- [A256012](https://oeis.org/A256012)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA256012


open Nat Finset

/--
a: Number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts that are not squarefree.
This is the number of finite subsets of positive integers $P$ such that
$\sum_{k \in P} k = n$ and every element $k \in P$ is not squarefree.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  -- The parts must be $\le n$ to sum to $n$.
  -- This is $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$
  let potential_parts : Finset ℕ := range (n + 1) \ {0}

  -- We count all subsets P of potential_parts that satisfy the sum and the property.
  card <| filter (fun P : Finset ℕ =>
    P.sum id = n ∧
    (∀ k ∈ P, ¬ Squarefree k)
  ) (powerset potential_parts)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide +kernel

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide +kernel

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by decide +kernel

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by decide +kernel


/--
Conjecture: $a(n) > 0$ for $n > 23$.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/256012.wip.lean#L91"]
theorem a_pos_of_gt (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 23) : a n > 0 := by
    sorry

end OeisA256012

reformulations.difference: OEIS defines a(n) as the number of partitions of n into distinct parts that are not squarefree. The Lean `a n` counts the Finsets P in the powerset of `range (n+1) \ {0}` = {1,…,n} with `P.sum id = n` and `∀ k ∈ P, ¬ Squarefree k`. It removes 0 from the candidate parts explicitly and does not use `Nat.Partition`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A partition of n into distinct parts is a multiset of positive integers with no repeats summing to n; every part is ≤ n. So it is exactly a subset of {1,…,n} with sum n, via P ↦ P.val with inverse p ↦ p.parts.toFinset. Removing 0 matters: Mathlib has `¬ Squarefree 0`, so otherwise 0 could be added to any valid set and every partition would be counted twice. `Squarefree 1` holds in Mathlib, matching OEIS, so 1 is never a part. I proved in Lean `a n = ((Nat.Partition.distincts n).filter (fun p => ∀ i ∈ p.parts, ¬ Squarefree i)).card` for all n with `Finset.card_bij'`, using only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Numerically, `a` matches the OEIS terms for n = 0..18 by `#eval`, and an independent DP matches the OEIS b-file for n = 0..400.

review.notes:
Declarations checked: `a`, `a_0`–`a_4`, `a_pos_of_gt`. All are faithful to OEIS A256012.

- Tests: a(0..4) = 1, 0, 0, 0, 1 match the OEIS data (offset 0).
- Main theorem: `a_pos_of_gt : ∀ n > 23, a n > 0` is exactly the OEIS comment "Conjecture: a(n) > 0 for n > 23". The bound is sharp: a(23) = 0, and the only zeros below 24 are at {1,2,3,5,6,7,10,11,14,15,19,23}. The b-file has no zeros for 24 ≤ n ≤ 10000.
- Status: OEIS now records the conjecture as proved by an autonomous AI agent (AlphaProof Nexus; arXiv 2605.22763), so `research solved` is correct.
- Proof claim: the AlphaProof Nexus file's `A256012` definition and `target_theorem_0` are character-for-character identical to the file's `a` and `a_pos_of_gt`. I adapted that proof (case split on n mod 4 with witnesses {n}, {9, n-9}, {18, n-18}, {27} or {27, n-27}) to the file's own `a`. It compiles with only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], which independently confirms the solved status.
- Formal-proof link not opened: the `formal_proof` attribute points to a commit in the fork github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures (`256012.wip.lean#L91`). I did not open it, to stay within the ban on consulting the formal-conjectures repository on GitHub. The same fork-link pattern with kind `formal_conjectures` appears in all 37 files from this arXiv batch. It is metadata, not mathematics.
